description.narrative: Mine action is a critical humanitarian need in Syria. The scale, severity, and complexity of the explosive ordnance threat in the country remains a major protection concern, compounding the humanitarian crisis and the vulnerability of civilians in affected areas. UNMAS estimates that since 2013, an average of six people per day have been killed or injured by explosive ordnance. According to the 2024 Humanitarian Needs Overview draft, 14.4 million men, women, and children are at risk from EO contamination. The destruction and contamination of residential areas and critical infrastructure, such as hospitals, schools and roads, hinders civilian access to basic services and the safe return of displaced persons. \nUNOPS supports the UNMAS humanitarian mine action intervention to mitigate the risk of explosive ordnance for communities and humanitarian workers through coordination, risk education and non-technical survey.
